purpose: Compare corpus-level retrieval, citation and cross-document answering for a repository of ANX files against a strong Markdown repository generated from the same canonical content, on a corpus of twelve freely downloadable public documents.

arms.anx-native-corpus: Typed ANX blocks, document metadata, revision-pinned stable citations, and typed relationship edges carried with the document.
arms.markdown-strong-corpus: One GFM Markdown file per document with YAML-style metadata, page-independent file/line citations, and equivalent declared relationship metadata. It is intentionally stronger than plain unstructured Markdown.

controls: Both arms use the same twelve public documents and the same canonical text produced by one import of each source.
Both arms use the same deterministic BM25-style lexical ranker, query limit (12), and per-document diversity cap (4).
The target document path is never supplied to corpus search; the model only sees tool output.
Source ANX packages are read-only and must remain byte-identical across the run.
Relationship fixtures are supplied equally to both arms and are labeled benchmark-series assertions.
No embedding model is used; semantic and vector retrieval are a separate treatment.
Live trials run in a fresh vanilla CLI session with no harness, memory, project files or web access, and may execute only the corpus tool.

qualification.statusMeaning: PASS qualifies benchmark integrity and both corpus transports. It does not establish ANX superiority.

models.tier: workhorse (continuity anchor with the private August 2026 run)

claimBoundary: This is a twelve-real-document corpus retrieval regime with a 240-logical-document deterministic scale probe and a small live answer smoke. It does not establish enterprise-scale production latency, vector-search quality, access-control behavior, human usability, universal parser quality, or a general ANX advantage over every Markdown RAG implementation.
